coverageNote: Disk enumeration matched the expected shape exactly: 11 units (the domain root directory plus 13.01-13.10) and 65 .md files. Every unit and every file was processed. Reading strategy, given ~1.29 MB of markdown across 65 files: (a) every index, CX-map, and small [SURFACE]/[PARTIAL] leaf was read in full; (b) the large [DEEP] leaves (13.01.01, 13.01.02, 13.01.04, 13.02.01, 13.02.02, 13.02.04, 13.03.01, 13.03.02, 13.05.01, 13.06.01, 13.06.02, 13.06.05, 13.08.01, 13.12) had their Behavior / Decisions / Open Questions sections read with long table cells truncated at 230-650 chars — Deep Think Annotations and Cross-Cut Notes on those files were read only in extract form; (c) every Decisions and Decision Log table in all 65 files was read; (d) every Open Questions row in all 65 files was machine-audited for owner + deferral target (all 214 rows pass); (e) status markers were machine-cross-checked between every index Children table and each child file's own header. Residual risk: contradictions buried in the truncated tail of a long Deep Think cell on one of the 14 largest leaves could have been missed. This tree is unusually well specified — decisions carry explicit rationale, calibration constants are declared as 'seeds' (decisions, not placeholders), and open questions are uniformly tracked with an owner and a pipeline-stage target — so the raw finding count is low by construction, not by sampling.

scoring.naRationale: Dimension 1 (Problem Clarity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, which are outside this domain's unit set. Scoring them here would either flatter the result (marking them auto-pass) or penalise absence of something never in scope. Dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity, via Role Matrix / Role Lens), 3 (Feature Completeness), 7 (Open Question Resolution) and 8 (Structural Compliance) apply to every unit and were scored.

findings.claim: The set of rules that may block a listing from publishing is enumerated four times across the domain, and the four enumerations are mutually exclusive. No marker, no open question, no owner covers the discrepancy. An implementer building the publish gate must invent which set is authoritative.
findings.evidence: gear-marketplace-index.md:115 — '| D-03 | **The listing flow never stalls** — every degradation publishes rather than blocks | Recurring across catalog matching, contribution, grading and disclosure. Two deliberate exceptions: material flaw photos (13.02.02 D-03) and CITES on international (13.07.03 D-02). |'  ||  13.03-listings-inventory/13.03.01-listing-creation-media-demo.md:27 — '**The governing rule is domain D-03: the flow never stalls.** Every degradation publishes. There are exactly two publish blockers in this flow and both are inherited, not invented here:'  ||  13.03-listings-inventory/13.03.01-listing-creation-media-demo.md:31 — '| Material flaw evidence missing | 13.02.02 D-03 | The single deliberate exception in the listing flow. ... |'  ||  13.03-listings-inventory/13.03.01-listing-creation-media-demo.md:222 — '| D-03 | Payout onboarding is the only hard publish prerequisite, and unsupported-country payout is surfaced at **draft start**, not at publish |'  ||  13.02-condition-originality-disclosure/13.02.02-mandatory-flaw-disclosure.md:165 — '| D-03 | Material flaws require evidence before publish — the only publish-blocking rule in the listing flow |'  ||  13.12-gear-seller-storefront-policies.md:126 — 'the storefront exists with policies and cannot publish a listing (13.03.01 D-03: no payout method is the flow's second and only other publish blocker)'
findings.failureScenario: A seller in a supported payout country lists a rosewood-fingerboard 1965 Martin with no material flaws disclosed and no payout method configured. Implementer A reads gear-marketplace-index.md D-03, implements exactly two publish exceptions {material-flaw evidence, CITES}, and publishes the listing with no payout method (a listing that can never be bought — the exact 'fictional listing' 13.03.01 D-03 exists to prevent). Implementer B reads 13.03.01 line 27 + D-03 and implements {material-flaw evidence, payout onboarding}, blocking publish, and never gates on CITES at listing time. Implementer C reads 13.02.02 D-03 or 13.03-listings-inventory-index.md D-01 literally ('the only publish-blocking rule' / 'The single exception is a material flaw photo') and implements exactly one blocker, publishing both the payout-less listing and the CITES-restricted one. Three different products from three internally-cited authorities.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether CITES restriction blocks listing publish or only blocks commitment gates (bid time / checkout), and whether payout onboarding is a member of the same exception set as material-flaw evidence or a separate category of prerequisite.

Two deliberate exceptions: material flaw photos (13.02.02 D-03) and CITES on international (13.07.03 D-02). | Breadth pass, **13.03 D-01** |' — the domain decision names 13.03 D-01 as its source, and 13.03 D-01 names one exception where the domain names two.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer working the 13.03 sub-domain in isolation (the normal decomposition boundary for /decompose-architecture) reads 13.03 D-01, implements a single publish exception, and ships a listing flow in which a CITES-restricted instrument publishes with no export-compliance gate anywhere in the listing path — while a reviewer working from the domain index expects the CITES exception to exist and finds it absent with no tracked question explaining the omission.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether CITES is or is not an exception to the never-stall rule at the listing layer.

findings.claim: The Excellent grade's Requires column imposes a repair-count limit that the Grade Ceilings table — declared to be 'a pure function of the disclosed flaw set' — cannot express and does not enforce. The two normative tables in the same file disagree on whether a unit with two professionally-repaired structural flaws may be Excellent.
findings.evidence: 13.02-condition-originality-disclosure/13.02.01-condition-grading-scale.md:39 — '| 3 | **Excellent** | Very light cosmetic deviation only — micro-scratches, faint playwear. No finish loss. | Asserted | Cosmetic flaws ≤ `light`; **at most one** professionally-executed, stable, disclosed structural repair |'  vs  13.02.01:55 — 'The cross-check is a **pure function** of the disclosed flaw set (13.02.02) → a ceiling. It never picks the grade; it bounds it.'  vs  13.02.01:63 — '| structural | `repaired` (professional, stable) | Ceiling: Excellent |'  vs  13.02.01:71 — 'The lowest applicable ceiling wins.'
findings.failureScenario: A seller lists a 1959 Les Paul with two disclosed structural repairs, both professionally executed and stable (a headstock repair and a neck reset — a routine pairing on a 60-year-old instrument). Implementer A implements the Ceilings table literally: each repair projects Ceiling: Excellent, the lowest applicable ceiling is Excellent, Excellent is offered and selected. Implementer B implements the Scale table's Requires column: 'at most one' is violated, so the ceiling drops to Good (the next value the Scale table permits). The same instrument grades Excellent on one build and Good on the other — a grade delta that, on a vintage Les Paul, is a five-figure price difference, and one that propagates into 13.04's comp set as a permanent distortion of the model × condition × originality bucket.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the flaw→ceiling projection is count-aware, and if so what ceiling a second professional structural repair projects to.

findings.claim: For an auction with ≥1 bid inside the final 12 hours, 13.02.01 E-14 mandates the exact action 13.03.02 D-10 prohibits. Neither statement carries a marker and no open question in either file covers the window.
findings.evidence: 13.02-condition-originality-disclosure/13.02.01-condition-grading-scale.md:105 — '| E-14 | **Downward regrade on an auction with ≥1 bid** | Grade cannot be edited downward. A bid was placed against a material fact; changing it under a live bid is not a correction, it is a bait-and-switch. **The auction must be cancelled** (13.05 owns cancellation) | "You can't lower the condition on a live auction with bids. Cancel the auction to regrade." |'  vs  13.03-listings-inventory/13.03.02-listing-lifecycle-relisting.md:245 — '| D-10 | An auction with ≥1 bid **cannot be seller-ended inside 12h of close**; earlier ends are permitted with a reason, notify all bidders, and count as a cancellation | Per DT-11. A seller who can walk at hour 11 makes bidding worthless. |'
findings.failureScenario: Eight hours before close, a seller running a 7-day auction on a Twin Reverb with 14 bids discovers the output transformer is failing — a functional flaw at `impaired`, which under the Grade Ceilings table forces the grade down from Excellent to Fair. E-14 forbids the downward edit and instructs 'cancel the auction to regrade'. D-10 forbids the seller from ending the auction at all inside 12h of close. Implementer A leaves the seller stuck: the auction runs to close and a binding sale completes on a description both parties now know is false. Implementer B treats the regrade as a platform-initiated cancellation exempt from D-10 (an invention — 13.05.02 specifies no cancellation path, and 13.03.02 D-10 is the only cancellation rule in the tree). Implementer C lets the downward edit through with a bidder notification, which is precisely the bait-and-switch E-14 exists to forbid.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a condition-driven cancellation is 'seller-ended' for the purposes of the 12-hour lockout, or a distinct platform-initiated termination with its own bidder-notification and reputation semantics.

findings.failureScenario: Downstream stages select work by depth status. /ideate-validate and /write-architecture-spec reading the domain index see a [SURFACE] node still owing a deepening pass and schedule one; reading the file itself they see [PARTIAL] — a node already deepened past surface, whose four remaining questions (Q-02 duty of care, Q-03 CX-M31 safeguarding, Q-04 off-platform provenance gap, Q-05 settled-branch residuals) are already routed to /create-prd-security and /write-be-spec. The node is either re-worked unnecessarily or its P-09/D-04 ratification is treated as less settled than it is.
